author: BLADE STAFF
title: Columbus offense takes off in 13-0 win over Mud Hens - NewsBreak
text: Visiting Columbus ambushed the Toledo Mud Hens for 13 runs over the five innings, resulting in a 13-0 shutout victory for the Clippers at Fifth Third Field on Wednesday. The game was scoreless through the first four innings, then Columbus (39-41) notched five-run innings in both the fifth and sixth to open up a 10-0 advantage on Toledo (42-41). In the fifth, most of the damage came via a Juan Brito grand slam. Milan Tolentino also had an RBI single in the inning. A trio of walks set up the Clippers in the sixth. Then after a lineout, Christian DeLauter doubled home a pair of runs for a 7-0 lead. Two batters later, C.J. Kayfus belted a three-run home run to right field that made it 10-0. Columbus continued to tack on with two more runs in the seventh. The Clippers opened the inning with base hits from Will Wilson, Petey Halpin, and Dom Nunez, followed by a Christian Cairo ground out to score Wilson (11-0). Tolentino followed with a sacrifice fly scoring Halpin for a 12-0 lead. In the eighth, Jhonkensy Noel, better known as “Big Christmas” by his Cleveland Guardians teammates, closed out the scoring with a solo homer to left-center. The Mud Hens scattered three hits throughout the game and committed an error. They were outhit by the Clippers 14-3. Akil Baddoo doubled in the home half of the first but was left stranded at third, Brewer Hicklen hit a one-out triple in the fourth, and Andrew Navigato led off the fifth with a single for Toledo. Vince Velasquez earned the win on the mound for Columbus, going 5⅔ innings, allowing no runs on three hits with eight strikeouts and just two walks. Toledo’s Wilkel Hernandez was the losing pitcher. He allowed five earned runs on six hits over 4⅔ innings of work. Hernandez had eight strikeouts as well. The Mud Hens and Clippers will square off at 7:05 p.m. Thursday at Fifth Third Field before the series shifts to Columbus for the final three games. Subscribe to The Blade
